industry.why: Neutral, carried, with the evidence moved towards the tape. Component 1 regime, 30-Oct-26 (risk-off beneath a steady index, led now by credit and the cost of debt rather than by the artificial intelligence wash-out alone: the US ten-year above 5% after a hawkish Fed hold with two dissents for a hike, Goldman Sachs' Risk Appetite Indicator at its lowest since April 2025, euro investment-grade and high-yield yields up 30 and 90 basis points since September, Brent near $115, the French premium a record 150 basis points, Europe rotating to quality, defensives and non-AI growth, the STOXX Europe 600 1.7% from its high with breadth recovering from the bottom fifth of three years and defensives leading cyclicals at four weeks and three months; sources present 2026-W44): third-quarter beats were sold (Sandvik down 5%, Atlas Copco down 8%, Hiab down 12%), Danske Bank's C-J (25 October) says 'a lot is priced in' with the order strength coming from data centres the market no longer pays for, and the exception is the non-AI compounder (Hexagon, 13% organic growth); against it, offshore services and nuclear have multi-year visibility and electrical equipment is still the physical bottleneck. Relative strength per 31-relative-strength.md, 2026-10-30 against 2026-08-28, not week on week: D now, C prior. The sector rows do the work: Electrical equipment, Diversified groups, Distributors, Test and measurement and Engineered components at C, Flow control and Building technology at D. Five live holdings (19.35 points of the book) sit here, judged in component 4. Counter-case for D: a tape that sells beats is a regime statement; for B: the order data remain the strongest non-AI demand read in the pack. To D on a second week of beats sold with relative strength falling to F.

memo.verdict: Neutral; park. Bodycote (BOY-GB) was a 'Major Corporate Change' case with an aerospace demand tailwind and someone else has completed it: a recommended cash offer at 940p per share from Vulcan Alpha Bidco (Veritas Capital), announced 2026-09-01, completion expected Q1 2027, caps the 'Modal return' from 910.5p (2026-10-05) at +3.2 percent in total, 2.2 percent a year over eighteen months and 1.1 percent a year over three years, below the framework's F threshold at every horizon. Conviction high on the return arithmetic (the offer is contractual; the spread is 3.2 percent), medium on the standalone case beneath it. The park is not forced by the gate (management B, business quality B, predictability B, trackability C); the 'Modal return' F forces it. The case reopens if the offer lapses and the shares trade at or below about 750p, where the standalone eighteen-month return approaches the 20 percent bar. A higher offer is rated unlikely (about one in ten) and even 960p would return only 5.4 percent.
case: - The internal change is real, broad and almost finished: new chief executive (May 2024) and chief financial officer (February 2023); group re-cut into Specialist Technologies, Precision Heat Treatment and Non-Core; 27 of 31 commodity sites exited; ten French automotive plants sold; £120m buyback done, £80m launched. Six of twelve internal forces strong against a threshold of three; the pass is on breadth, since the 2028 targets (margin above 20 percent, ST 35 to 40 percent of revenue, ROCE 15 to 20 percent, cash conversion 80 to 90 percent) were reconfirmed in 2026, not raised; the one raise is the Optimise run-rate benefit to at least £15m by mid-2027.

- The external change is a net tailwind on the high-margin half: A&D +24.6 percent in H1 2026 on LEAP build rates and military flight hours, backlog-evidenced with two-plus years' visibility and two US Tier 1 long-term agreements renewed; IGT +11.0 percent on data-centre power with double digits guided for six to eighteen months; defence pipeline in Germany above ten times annual sales; EU ETS and REACH push outsourcing. Against: Automotive -4.4 percent, structural in Western Europe; 44 percent of revenue flat or contracting; Western Europe about 50 percent of revenue with PMIs below 50.

- The change has travelled all six layers of the 'Six Layer Inputs-outputs' chain, the last least: core organic +9.6 percent, margin +110 basis points to 16.0 percent, adjusted EPS +18.3 percent to 25.2p; sell-side FY2026 EPS +2.2 percent over six months and -1.7 percent over twelve. A 7 percent EBIT beat produced a 1 to 2 percent upgrade because H2 2026 is guided to moderate on comparatives (+3.2 percent core organic in H2 2025 vs -3.5 percent in H1 2025).
counter_case: - At its strongest (BB1): the offer undervalues the business. Deutsche Bank (2026-03-30): civil aerospace alone covers 82 percent of enterprise value at mid-cycle multiples; non-A&D Bodycote trades at about 1x EV/EBIT. A&D is about half of group operating profit, growing 24.6 percent; Specialist Technologies margins of 26.1 percent rival US aerospace suppliers on 25x to 49x forward earnings (Curtiss-Wright, HEICO); targets of 960p (Deutsche Bank) and 950p (RBC, Hold) sit above the offer; a holder should ride for a bump or through a lapse for the sum-of-the-parts re-rating.

- Record's response: the cover tested like for like (divisional EBIT vs EV multiple). A&D EBIT about £61m of FY2026 consensus EBIT 122 GBPm. At about 16x EV/EBIT (the house's own implied multiple) that is about £976m, 53 percent of the £1,852m offer EV; at Morgan Advanced Materials' 8.9x, about £543m, 29 percent. An 82 percent cover needs about 25x EV/EBIT on A&D, a US aerospace-supplier multiple, not a UK industrial one. Concession: the mix argues for a multiple above the ten-year median, and at the conceded 15.2x the lapse branch returns 16.3 percent a year over eighteen months, still below the bar from today's price; the offer is full by the stock's history and modest by aerospace peers'. Held because a bump is unlikely with the rival gone and the board committed, and 960p returns 5.4 percent; the hypothesis is a reason the acquirer pays 940p, not a reason to pay 910.5p.
triggers: - What reopens the case: the offer lapsing and the shares at or below about 750p (standalone eighteen-month return approaches the bar at about 752p; three-year at 642p).

- What changes the modal view: a Rule 2.4 announcement from a third party (none in the files); a second-phase regulatory review announced, or the scheme timetable slipping past Q1 2027 (Alarm); the scheme lapsing (Invalidate for the completion driver and the re-rating leg).

- Lapse-branch tests: FY2026 margin below 16.5 percent; core organic growth below +3.0 percent for two periods; retained volume from exited sites below 20 percent; net debt above 1.2x EBITDA; LTA volume retention below 95 percent; a LEAP or GTF build-schedule cut above 10 percent for FY2027 to FY2028 (Invalidate for the aerospace driver); European PMIs below 45; classical plant utilisation below 65 percent for two quarters; sell-side cuts of 2 percent or more.

- Unknowns in the files: whether the 7.2p interim is paid before completion; whether the £80m buyback runs during the offer period; the jurisdictions of regulatory clearance; dates of shareholder and court meetings and of the next trading update; the raise-to-lower revision count; top-five market share; return on tangible capital; plant utilisation and surcharge realisation (not disclosed).

- To test outside this folder: the five plausible overlaps with the framework's own historical errors (bid-inflated entry for a fundamental case; one hot segment masking erosion; restructuring gains as exclusions; unanimous sell-side bullishness; a "takeover floor" that is a ceiling) against the track-record and lessons files and the Wisdom Library; the expert claims of 0.1 percent operational margin gain and shop-floor paperwork mismatches, first if the offer fails.

- Store housekeeping: once the three fixed 'Modal return' lines are in the ratings store, Master Rating 8 is expected to re-base from D to F while the offer stands; the store's mapped B, B, B, C for Bodycote were not read before this record and the agreement is coincidence.
